desc:
An AI tool review of your current software finds the AI features you already pay for and the subscriptions that overlap. Ecom Swift LLC checks each tool you send and gives you a simple table with a keep, change or drop note for every one.

## What is an AI tool review?

An AI tool review is a check of the software your business already uses, done to find out which AI features each product includes, which of them your team could use today and which tools duplicate each other. It looks at the tools you have, before you consider buying anything new.

The result is a one page table, not a long report, so you can act on it quickly.

## Why you may already own what you are about to buy

Software makers add AI features to their products often. Email platforms add writing help, design tools add image options, accounting and help desk tools add summaries and suggested replies. Many of these sit unused because nobody announced them, or because they live on a higher plan or behind a setting that is switched off.

Meanwhile, subscriptions pile up. Two tools may do the same job because different people bought them at different times. A review catches both problems: features you have not used and money spent twice.

## How a review improves your results

A review lowers cost and raises use. If a feature you already pay for can do the job, you avoid a new subscription. If two tools overlap, you can drop one and reduce the bill. If a tool is weak, you learn about better fitting alternatives before the next renewal.

It also helps your team. A clear list of features they can switch on today means quick improvements without training on a new product. People already know the interface, so adoption is easier. Savings depend on your plans and renewal terms, so we show where to look and let you confirm the figures with each vendor.

## What a thorough tool review includes

- A full list of the tools you use and what each one costs.
- The AI features each tool offers, in plain words.
- Which of those features your team could use right now.
- The plan or setting each feature depends on.
- Overlaps, where two tools do the same job.
- Gaps, where a task has no good tool.
- A keep, change or drop note for each tool.
- Alternatives for weaker tools, in the larger packages.
- Notes on data and privacy for each tool.
- A short list of next steps in the order to do them.

## How we carry out the review

You send a list of your tools, with the plan and monthly or yearly cost of each if you know it. We check the public information each vendor publishes, including feature lists and plan descriptions, and compare them with how you use the tool.

We then build the table. The Basic package covers a smaller set of tools with the AI features listed and overlaps marked. Standard handles more tools, checks plan and cost, lists features you could switch on today and adds a short set of next steps. Premium covers a complete stack, suggests alternatives for weak tools, estimates the yearly cost and saving, adds privacy notes and ends with a results call. Add-ons include extra tools, a guide for staff on the features found and a renewal calendar so you know when to decide.

The review is research and advice. We do not change settings in your accounts.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Include every paid tool, even small ones.
- Note who uses each tool and how often.
- Check renewal dates before you act on a recommendation.
- Turn on one new feature at a time and test it.
- Ask each vendor to confirm what your plan includes.

**Avoid:**
- Cancelling a tool before checking what depends on it.
- Assuming a higher plan is needed without checking.
- Buying a new AI product before using the features you own.
- Turning on features that process customer data without reading how they handle it.
- Letting a renewal pass while a better option waits.

## Who this is for

This service suits an owner who suspects the company pays for too many subscriptions. It suits a manager who has been asked to cut software costs without hurting the team. It also suits a business that is about to buy an AI product and wants to be sure nothing it already owns could do the job.

We also review tools that are not well known, as long as the vendor publishes enough information about them. Where the information is thin, we say so in the review.

## What we need from you

A list of your tools, the plan you are on and what you pay, if you have it. A few words on what each tool is used for help us judge fit. We never ask for passwords and we do not log into your accounts. Reviews are done from the lists you send and the vendors' public information. Where a detail is unclear, we may ask for a screenshot of a plan page.
